every_position_composed.reason: Site 2 keeps its 3D workbench cleanly framed on the right across frames 1 to 9 with smooth camera travel, whereas Site 1 obscures its 3D chamber behind scrolling cards in frames 2 and 3 and leaves an almost empty scene in frame 6.

explains_the_project.reason: Site 2 turns the pipeline into a clear visual diagram—compressing a massive red-and-grey log slab through a press into a small digest with a yellow needle in frames 3 and 4, filing it in a cabinet in frame 5, and routing to seven harness lanes in frame 8.

craft_of_the_3d.reason: Site 1 exhibits richer metallic and emissive materials, specular highlights, and dynamic lighting on its chamber, caliper, and router in frames 1, 5, and 7, while Site 2 relies on flatter shading and simple colored blocks.

type_and_layout.reason: Site 2 uses concise, well-proportioned cards pinned cleanly to the top-left across all 9 frames to give the 3D scene room, while Site 1 crowds the viewport with tall, dense panels that clip at the edges in frames 3, 6, and 7 and hide the 3D entirely in frames 8 and 9.

overall.reason: Site 2 delivers a far more cohesive scroll choreography and an intuitive visual metaphor that genuinely helps a visitor see how Straitjacket compresses logs, stores artifacts, and coordinates harnesses without text crowding out the 3D stage.
